liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Dancing In The Streets** (1 review): Reviewer loves this version, especially the tom tom fills played during its jam section [5]
- **New Orleans** (1 review): New Orleans emerges directly out of the drums within Good Lovin' [5]
- **Alligator** (1 review): A Darkness, Darkness jam follows Alligator; it is one of only a handful of shows with it [6]
- **Drums** (1 review): The jam coming out of the second Drums segment is called unbelievable; Good Lovin', Alligator and China>Rider also stand out [13]
- **Dancin In The Streets** (1 review): Reviewer praises its excellent jamming and slow groove; rest of show is called solid but unremarkable [16]

## Setlist highlights

- **New Orleans**: rare: 5 archived performances [17]
- **Turn On Your Lovelight reprise**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [17]

## The recordings

- **gd70-06-06.sbd.ashley.2172.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 20 songs; 137 min; rated 4.18/5 by 17 [1]. Said about its sound: Sound is not fantastic but still sharp for its age; a few cuts appear; Pigpen features heavily; Few good soundboards survive from summer 1970, which makes this one worth getting [5][10]
- **gd1970-06-06.132487.sbd.bear.latvala.wise.flac16**: soundboard; 20 songs; 138 min; rated 4.17/5 by 6 [2]
- **gd1970-06-06.sbd.miller.86951.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 20 songs; 137 min; rated 3.94/5 by 18 [3]
- **gd1970-06-06.132157.miller.sbd.flac16**: soundboard; 4 songs; 19 min; rated 3.25/5 by 4 [4]

## Around the show

- Attendee of six 1970 Fillmore West shows recalls one where Alligator opened with kazoos, and Garcia soloed with heavy sustain [9]
- Show took place about a month after the Kent State student deaths, amid uncertainty and paranoia [10]
- This is the only mid-1970 Fillmore West Alligator listed on the archive; the opening solo resembles the Feb. 14, 1968 one [9]
- Fun show, but not among the truly elite gigs of 1970 [11]
- Reviewer ranks it in the top five of summer 1970 shows; later shows moved to Fillmore East [12]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd70-06-06.sbd.ashley.2172.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Jay Ashley; source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Reviewer doubts Bear's claim that nobody else taped the shows, noting audience tapes of the period exist; Source is a soundboard reel master transferred to cassette, then DAT, then CD, then SHN [1][8]
- **gd1970-06-06.132487.sbd.bear.latvala.wise.flac16**: taped by Bear; transferred by Dick Latvala and Jim Wise; source: 7 Inch Half Track Reel Master @ 7.5 ips(Recorded By Bear on a Sony 770 Reel 2 Reel)- 1st Generation Cassettes (TDK SAX-100's) Transferred By Dick… [2]
- **gd1970-06-06.sbd.miller.86951.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Cassette -> Dat -> CD [3]
- **gd1970-06-06.132157.miller.sbd.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Dat -> CD [4]
